scientific_quote: Labrador Retrievers showed consistently elevated hip dysplasia prevalence across multi-breed genetic validation cohorts.
A POMC gene deletion was strongly associated with increased weight and obesity prevalence in Labrador Retriever dogs.
Golden Retrievers had the highest risk of CHD diagnosis among guide dog breeding program cohorts.
Golden Retrievers demonstrated elevated atopic dermatitis prevalence linked to environmental allergen seropositivity.
Siberian Huskies presented with hereditary cataracts at higher rates than non-Arctic breed comparators in multicenter retrospective data.
Northern spitz-type breeds carried distinct genetic markers associated with immune-mediated skin disease susceptibility.
Chondrodystrophic breeds including Welsh Corgis carried the FGF4 retrogene driving elevated intervertebral disc disease risk.
Smaller chondrodystrophic breeds retained measurable hip dysplasia prevalence in radiographic screening programs.
French Bulldogs exhibited high brachycephalic obstructive airway syndrome prevalence across multi-breed cross-sectional data.
Brachycephalic dogs were twenty times more likely to develop corneal ulceration than non-brachycephalic controls.
Pugs showed among the highest BOAS prevalence rates of all brachycephalic breeds evaluated in cross-sectional screening.
Brachycephalic skull conformation and dental crowding substantially increased periodontal disease prevalence in small breeds.
German Shepherd Dogs retained elevated hip dysplasia prevalence in across-breed genetic marker validation studies.
German Shepherd Dogs carried a high SOD1 mutant allele frequency linked to degenerative myelopathy susceptibility.
Chronic enteropathy represented a substantial gastrointestinal disease burden across hound and companion breed populations.
Small and toy breed dogs carried the highest degenerative mitral valve disease prevalence in primary-care veterinary populations.
